newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ fixed rates on way down, REINZ says.
newsitem.headline: NZ fixed rates on way down, REINZ says.

text.p: Fixed home lending rates have continued to fall in the last month, with 20 of 28 institutions either reducing rates or introducing new fixed or capped rates in the last month, the Real Estate Institute's monthly survey published on Thursday has found.
However, no lending institution reduced its floating rate during the period.
Institute president Colin Brown said the downward trend in fixed rates was most noticeable in terms of two to three years.

"Competition for the mortgage market continues to intensify with 13 lenders now offering two year fixed rates at 9.90 percent. Three other institutions now have a two year fixed rate of 9.75 percent," he said.
Last month, only one institution was offering a fixed rate at under 10 percent.

Floating interest rates in October ranged between 10.85 percent and 11.5 percent and fixed rates between 9.5 percent and 10.5 percent for six months, 9.95 percent and 10.75 percent for one year, and 9.75 percent and 10.5 percent for three years.
Fifteen institutions offered one year capped loans at rates between 9.95 percent and 11.5 percent.
Several lenders were making special offers and cash draws at the moment, Brown said.
